acceptance.summary: The periodic security workflow now pins cargo-fuzz and its dedicated nightly, fails closed, preserves corpus and crash artifacts, separates bounded compilation and fuzz-runtime deadlines, and builds the required ccos binary explicitly under Rust 1.89 for reproducibility.
verified_properties: cargo-fuzz 0.13.2 is installed with --locked under nightly-2026-09-28.
The fuzz crate is an explicit independent workspace with its dedicated toolchain and lockfile.
No forced-success operator remains; crash, finding, launch error, compile timeout or runtime timeout fails the job.
Fuzz-target compilation is bounded at 300 seconds and the 60-second libFuzzer campaign has an independent 90-second outer deadline.
Corpus and crash paths are retained for 30 days even when the fuzz step fails.
Reproducibility builds use Rust 1.89.0 and --features llm --bin ccos twice from clean state, then compare hashes.
Workflow actions introduced or touched by the remediation are pinned to full commit SHAs.
limitations: The 60-second smoke campaign is bounded regression evidence, not exhaustive fuzzing or production qualification.
GitHub-hosted Ubuntu execution does not qualify other operating systems or specialized hardware.
No product boundary, replay semantics, storage format, license or excluded repository was changed.

failure_history.reason: The fuzz manifest was below the root workspace without membership or an independent workspace.
A single 120-second outer timeout included approximately 103 seconds of compilation and interrupted the nominal 60-second campaign after approximately 17 seconds with exit code 124.

counting.rule: Count the technical PR exactly once; do not count tracker-only evidence commits.
